t.1.20.1: The Sūta said: Having crossed over that ocean, Kadrū, swift-moving, together with Vinatā, alighted near the horse before long.
t.1.20.2: And seeing the many black hairs clinging to the tail, Kadrū put Vinatā, whose face was downcast with dejection, into servitude.
t.1.20.3: Then Vinatā, defeated in that wager, was consumed by sorrow and entered into the state of a slave.
t.1.20.4: Meanwhile, when the time had come, the greatly splendid Garuḍa split open the egg and was born without his mother.
t.1.20.5: Blazing forth like a heap of fire, kindled and exceedingly terrifying, the bird of enormous body suddenly grew great and rose into the sky.
t.1.20.6: Seeing him, all creatures went for refuge to Vibhāvasu, and bowing down they spoke to him as he sat there, he whose form is the universe.
t.1.20.9: Thus addressed, the gods together with the hosts of seers then went forth and, approaching him from not far off, praised Garuḍa with words.
t.1.20.8: It is not as you suppose, O tormentors of the asuras. This is the mighty Garuḍa, equal to me in his own splendor.
t.1.20.7: O Agni, do not grow any further. Surely you do not wish to burn us at all? For that vast, blazing mass of yours is spreading.
t.1.20.10: You are a seer, you are the greatly blessed one, you are a god, the lord of birds; you are the master, radiant like the sun, you are our unsurpassed refuge.
t.1.20.11: You alone are surging with waves of strength, virtuous, of undaunted spirit, prosperous and irresistible; O you of undiminished fame, you are all austerity and sacred learning, all that is yet to come and all that has come to pass.
t.1.20.12: You are supreme; like the sun with its rays, you illumine all this world of moving and unmoving things. Repeatedly eclipsing the radiance of the sun, you are the Ender of all this, the lasting and the fleeting.
t.1.20.14: Having approached Garuḍa, lord of birds, of mighty energy, free of darkness, ranging through the clouds, of great strength, sky-goer, the highest and the lowest, bestower of boons, of unconquerable valor, we have come to him for refuge.
t.1.20.13: As the enraged sun would burn all creatures, so do you burn, O you whose radiance is like fire; you are terrifying, like fire risen up at the dissolution, destroying all, bringing the end at the turning of the yuga.
t.1.20.15: Thus praised then by the gods together with the hosts of seers, Suparṇa withdrew his own blazing splendor.
